questions.question_english: According to the statutory rules and standard operating procedures (SOPs) framed under the RPwD Act, 2016, what is the maximum time frame generally stipulated for a Grievance Redressal Officer to inquire into and resolve a complaint filed by an employee with a disability?
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 23 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 and Rule 10 of the RPwD Rules, 2017, read with administrative instructions and SOPs issued by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) and the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), the Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) must inquire into the complaint and take up the matter with the head of the establishment for corrective action. questions.question_english: Within the mandated 4% reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in public employment under Section 34 of the RPwD Act, 2016, what specific percentage is allocated to the category of 'deaf and hard of hearing'?
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 34(1) of the RPwD Act, 2016, the overall 4% reservation in government vacancies is compartmentalized across five specific disability groups as follows:
(a) Blindness and low vision: 1%
(b) Deaf and hard of hearing: 1%
(c) Locomotor disability including cerebral palsy, leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims, and muscular dystrophy: 1%
(d) Autism, intellectual disability, specific learning disability, and mental illness: combined with (e) Multiple disabilities from amongst persons under clauses (a) to (d) including deafblindness: 1%

Together, categories (a), (b), (c) receive 1% each, and combined categories (d) and (e) receive 1%, making up the total 4% reservation. Thus, the category of deaf and hard of hearing is allotted exactly 1%.

Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The Constitution of India empowers the State to grant consequential seniority to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe employees promoted through reservation rosters.
Reason (R): The Constitution (Eighty-Fifth Amendment) Act, 2001 inserted the words "with consequential seniority" into Article 16(4A) with retrospective effect from 17th June 1995.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A):

1. Background to 'Catch-Up Rule': In Union of India v. Virpal Singh Chauhan (1995) and Ajit Singh Januja v. State of Punjab (1996 & 1999), the Supreme Court evolved the 'catch-up rule', holding that roster-point reserved category promotees do not automatically get consequential seniority over senior general candidates who catch up to them in the promotional cadre.

2. Constitutional Amendment: To negate the 'catch-up rule' and restore consequential seniority to SC/ST promotees, Parliament enacted the Constitution (Eighty-Fifth Amendment) Act, 2001. This amendment modified Article 16(4A) by substituting the words 'in matters of promotion to any class' with 'in matters of promotion, with consequential seniority, to any class', with retrospective effect from 17 June 1995 (the date of the 77th Amendment).

3. Constitutional Validity: In M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006), a 5-judge Constitution Bench upheld the validity of the 85th Amendment and consequential seniority, confirming that it does not destroy the basic structure of the Constitution provided the concepts of backwardness, inadequacy of representation, and administrative efficiency (Article 335) are maintained.

Thus, (R) directly explains why the State has the constitutional power stated in (A).

1. 'कैच-अप नियम' (Catch-up Rule) की पृष्ठभूमि: वीरपाल सिंह चौहान (1995) और अजीत सिंह जनूजा (1996 व 1999) मामलों में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने प्रतिपादित किया था कि आरक्षण रोस्टर के तहत पदोन्नत आरक्षित श्रेणी के कर्मचारी सामान्य वर्ग के अपने वरिष्ठ साथियों पर परिणामी वरिष्ठता का दावा नहीं कर सकते, यदि सामान्य वर्ग का कर्मचारी बाद में पदोन्नत होकर उस उच्च पद पर पहुँच जाता है (कैच-अप कर लेता है)।

2. 85वां संविधान संशोधन: इस कैच-अप नियम को निरस्त करने तथा SC/ST कर्मचारियों को परिणामी वरिष्ठता का लाभ देने के लिए संसद ने संविधान (85वां संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2001 पारित किया। इसके द्वारा अनुच्छेद 16(4A) में 17 जून 1995 (77वें संशोधन की तिथि) से भूतलक्षी प्रभाव से "परिणामी वरिष्ठता सहित" (with consequential seniority) शब्दावली अंतःस्थापित की गई।

3. संवैधानिक वैधता: 'एम. नागराज बनाम भारत संघ (2006)' मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की 5-न्यायाधीशों की संविधान पीठ ने 85वें संशोधन की वैधता को बरकरार रखा।

questions.explanation_english: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 marks an essential paradigm shift from the medical and charity-oriented approach of the 1995 legislation to a human rights-based and social model. The medical model viewed disability as an individual physical or mental deficit needing medical treatment, charity, or pity. In contrast, the rights-based social model, aligned with UNCRPD and Articles 14, 15, and 21 of the Indian Constitution, recognizes that disability is the outcome of the interaction between individuals with impairments and systemic environmental, institutional, and attitudinal barriers that hinder their full, equal, and dignified participation in society.

questions.explanation_english: Under Sections 56, 57, and 58 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 read with the RPwD Rules, 2017, the power to assess disability and issue a certificate of benchmark disability is vested exclusively in the notified 'certifying authority'. questions.question_english:
Consider the following duties and measures prescribed for educational institutions under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016:
I. Providing reasonable accommodation according to the individual's requirements.
II. Providing transportation facilities to children with disabilities and to the attendants of children with high support needs.
III. Ensuring early detection of specific learning disabilities and taking pedagogical measures to address them.
IV. Supplying specialized uniforms free of cost to all students with disabilities.
Which of the duties given above are legally mandated under the Act?
questions.explanation_english:
Statements I, II, and III are statutory mandates under Chapter III (Education) of the RPwD Act, 2016, whereas Statement IV is not:

- Statement I is correct: Section 16(iii) requires institutions to 'provide reasonable accommodation according to the individual's requirements'.
- Statement II is correct: Section 16(viii) mandates institutions to 'provide transportation facilities to the children with disabilities and also the attendant of the children with disabilities having high support needs'.
- Statement III is correct: Section 17(d) directs the appropriate government and local authorities to establish mechanisms to 'detect specific learning disabilities in children at the earliest and take suitable pedagogical and other measures to overcome them'.
- Statement IV is incorrect: While Section 16(vii) mandates the supply of books, learning materials, and appropriate assistive devices free of cost up to the age of 18 years, the statute does not mandate supplying 'specialized uniforms free of cost'.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I, II और III दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 के अध्याय III (शिक्षा) के अंतर्गत कानूनी रूप से अनिवार्य हैं, जबकि कथन IV अधिनियम में सम्मिलित नहीं है:

- कथन I सही है: धारा 16(iii) के अनुसार प्रत्येक बच्चे की व्यक्तिगत आवश्यकता के अनुसार समुचित वास-सुविधा (Reasonable accommodation) प्रदान करना अनिवार्य है।
- कथन II सही है: धारा 16(viii) स्पष्ट रूप से आदेश देती है कि शिक्षण संस्थान 'दिव्यांग बच्चों को तथा उच्च सहायता की आवश्यकता वाले बच्चों के सहायकों (attendants) को भी परिवहन सुविधाएं प्रदान करेंगे'।
- कथन III सही है: धारा 17(d) सरकार और स्थानीय प्राधिकरणों को यह दायित्व सौंपती है कि वे बच्चों में विशिष्ट अधिगम अक्षमता (SLD) की शीघ्र पहचान करें तथा उपयुक्त शैक्षणिक उपाय अपनाएं।
- कथन IV गलत है: धारा 16(vii) के तहत 18 वर्ष की आयु तक निःशुल्क पुस्तकें, शिक्षण सामग्री और उपयुक्त सहायक उपकरण (Assistive devices) प्रदान करने का दायित्व है, परंतु 'निःशुल्क विशिष्ट वर्दी' प्रदान करने का कोई विधिक आदेश नहीं है।

questions.question_english: Under the Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, under which of the following broad classifications is 'Deafblindness' categorized?
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Schedule of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 (specifying disabilities under Section 2(zc)), disabilities are broadly organized into specified categories including Physical Disability, Intellectual Disability, Mental Illness, Disabilities caused by Chronic Neurological Conditions & Blood Disorders, and Multiple Disabilities.

Section 2(zc) read with the Schedule defines 'Multiple Disabilities' as the occurrence of more than one of the specified disabilities in an individual, explicitly including 'Deafblindness'. Deafblindness is characterized as a distinct condition caused by a combination of both severe visual and hearing impairments, creating severe communication, developmental, educational, and mobility challenges. It cannot be accommodated simply as a single sensory impairment, which is why Parliament designated it under the Multiple Disabilities category to ensure specialized rehabilitation, tactile communication methods, and assistive pedagogical aids in educational institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 2(zc) के साथ पठित अनुसूची (Schedule) में विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं (Specified Disabilities) को विभिन्न श्रेणियों में वर्गीकृत किया गया है। इनमें शारीरिक दिव्यांगता, बौद्धिक दिव्यांगता, मानसिक रुग्णता, दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी एवं रक्त विकार तथा 'बहु-दिव्यांगता' शामिल हैं।

अनुसूची के पैरा 5 के अंतर्गत 'बहु-दिव्यांगता' (Multiple Disabilities) के तहत दो या दो से अधिक विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं के संयोजन को शामिल किया गया है, जिसमें स्पष्ट रूप से 'बधिर-अंधता' (Deafblindness) का उल्लेख किया गया है। बधिर-अंधता दृष्टि और श्रवण दोनों प्रकार की गंभीर क्षतियों का ऐसा मिला-जुला रूप है जिसके कारण गंभीर संचार, विकासात्मक और अधिगम संबंधी बाधाएं उत्पन्न होती हैं। इसलिए कानून में इसे एकल संवेदी बाधा न मानकर 'बहु-दिव्यांगता' के अंतर्गत रखा गया है ताकि ऐसे शिक्षार्थियों को विशेष स्पर्श संचार (स्पर्श ब्रेल), अनुरूपित शिक्षण और पुनर्वास सेवाएं प्रदान की जा सकें।

Under the Schedule of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016, deafblindness is categorized under the broader classification of multiple disabilities, which covers combination of two or more specified disabilities occurring simultaneously in an individual.

Consider the following statements regarding the verification of caste/community certificates during government teacher recruitment:
I. The appointing authority must verify the caste certificate through the District Magistrate or competent issuing authority before offering a permanent appointment.
II. A provisional appointment can be offered subject to the subsequent verification of the caste certificate.
III. If the caste certificate is found to be false or fabricated, the services of the teacher are terminated without any further notice and penal action is initiated.
IV. The burden of proving the authenticity of the caste certificate lies solely with the school Principal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation_english:
According to the Supreme Court judgment in Kumari Madhuri Patil v. Additional Commissioner (1994) and DoPT Office Memoranda (e.g., OM No. 36011/1/2012-Estt.(Res)) regarding verification of caste certificates:

questions.question_english: In the landmark judgment of Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022), a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court upheld the validity of the 103rd Constitutional Amendment. What was the core legal holding of the majority regarding the 'Basic Structure' doctrine?
options_english: Economic criteria alone can never form a constitutionally valid basis for affirmative action
Providing EWS reservation beyond the 50% ceiling breaches and destroys the basic structure of the Constitution
Providing reservation solely based on economic criteria preserves and does not violate the basic structure of the Constitution
EWS reservation must mandatorily include SC, ST, and OBC communities to avoid violating the basic structure
questions.explanation_english:
In Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (Writ Petition (Civil) No. 55 of 2019, decided in November 2022), a 5-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of the 103rd Constitutional Amendment by a 3:2 majority (Justices Dinesh Maheshwari, Bela M. Trivedi, and J.B. Pardiwala in majority; CJI U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissenting).

The majority held that:
1. Reservation structured solely on economic criteria does not violate the Basic Structure of the Constitution. Affirmative action is not restricted solely to socially and educationally backward classes.
2. The exclusion of SCs, STs, and OBCs from EWS reservation does not violate the equality code or destroy the basic structure because they already receive benefits under compensatory discrimination under Articles 15(4), 15(5), and 16(4).
3. The 50% ceiling rule laid down in Indra Sawhney (1992) applies to existing vertical reservations for backward classes under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) and is not inflexible; exceeding it for EWS does not damage the basic structure of the Constitution.
questions.explanation_hindi:
जनहित अभियान बनाम भारत संघ (2022) के ऐतिहासिक मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की 5-सदस्यीय संविधान पीठ ने 3:2 के बहुमत से 103वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम की संवैधानिक वैधता को बरकरार रखा (न्यायमूर्ति दिनेश माहेश्वरी, न्यायमूर्ति बेला एम. त्रिवेदी और न्यायमूर्ति जे.बी. पारदीवाला बहुमत में थे; जबकि तत्कालीन मुख्य न्यायाधीश यू.यू. ललित और न्यायमूर्ति एस. रवींद्र भट असहमत थे)।

बहुमत के मुख्य विधिक निष्कर्ष निम्नलिखित थे:
1. केवल आर्थिक मानदंडों के आधार पर आरक्षण प्रदान करना संविधान के बुनियादी ढांचे (Basic Structure) का उल्लंघन नहीं करता है, क्योंकि राज्य की सकारात्मक कार्रवाई केवल सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक पिछड़ेपन तक ही सीमित नहीं है।
2. EWS कोटे से एससी, एसटी और ओबीसी को बाहर रखना समानता के सिद्धांत का उल्लंघन नहीं करता, क्योंकि वे पहले से ही अनुच्छेद 15(4), 15(5) और 16(4) के तहत आरक्षण का लाभ प्राप्त कर रहे हैं।
3. इंदिरा साहनी (1992) मामले में निर्धारित 50% की आरक्षण सीमा अनम्य (inflexible) नहीं है और यह मुख्य रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों के लिए थी; EWS आरक्षण द्वारा इसका पार होना बुनियादी ढांचे को नष्ट नहीं करता है।

questions.question_english: What is the specific statutory term defined in Section 2(m) of the RPwD Act, 2016 for an educational system where students with and without disabilities learn together and the system of teaching and learning is suitably adapted?
questions.explanation_english:
Section 2(m) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 defines 'inclusive education' as:
'a system of education wherein students with and without disability learn together and the system of teaching and learning is suitably adapted to meet the learning needs of different types of students with disabilities.'

This marks a profound pedagogical shift from 'Special Education' (which isolates students with disabilities into segregated institutions) and 'Integrated Education' (which places disabled children in general schools without adapting the underlying curriculum or infrastructure). Inclusive education demands systematic restructuring of physical classrooms, pedagogical materials, teacher training, and assistive aids to foster universal accessibility and belonging.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 2(m) में 'समावेशी शिक्षा' (Inclusive Education) को स्पष्ट रूप से परिभाषित किया गया है:
'समावेशी शिक्षा से ऐसी शिक्षा प्रणाली अभिप्रेत है जिसमें दिव्यांगता वाले और दिव्यांगता रहित विद्यार्थी एक साथ सीखते हैं और शिक्षण एवं सीखने की प्रणाली को विभिन्न प्रकार के दिव्यांग विद्यार्थियों की अधिगम आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने के लिए उपयुक्त रूप से अनुकूलित किया जाता है।'

यह संकल्पना 'विशेष शिक्षा' (जिसमें दिव्यांग बच्चों को अलग विशेष स्कूलों में रखा जाता है) और 'एकीकृत शिक्षा' (जिसमें बिना पाठ्यक्रम बदले बच्चे को केवल सामान्य स्कूल में बैठा दिया जाता है) से भिन्न और श्रेष्ठ है। समावेशी शिक्षा विद्यालयी वातावरण, पाठ्यक्रम, शिक्षण विधियों और मूल्यांकन में सर्वांगीण अनुकूलन की मांग करती है।

questions.question_english: The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to arrest dropouts after elementary education. From which grade onwards is the scholarship financial assistance actually disbursed?
questions.explanation_english: The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by the Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education. The scheme conducts a nationwide selection examination consisting of a Mental Ability Test (MAT) and Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT) for students studying in Class VIII in government and government-aided schools. Once selected in Class VIII, the actual financial disbursement of the scholarship—amounting to ₹12,000 per annum (₹1,000 per month)—begins from Class IX onwards and continues through Classes X, XI, and XII (for a total duration of 4 years), subject to the recipient securing at least 55% marks and continuing their studies in recognized state government or local body schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: 'राष्ट्रीय साधन-सह-योग्यता छात्रवृत्ति योजना' (NMMSS) केंद्रीय शिक्षा मंत्रालय के स्कूल शिक्षा और साक्षरता विभाग द्वारा संचालित एक केंद्र प्रायोजित योजना है। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्गों (EWS) के मेधावी छात्रों को कक्षा 8 के बाद पढ़ाई छोड़ने (ड्रॉपआउट) से रोकना है। इस योजना हेतु चयन परीक्षा (MAT और SAT) कक्षा 8 में आयोजित की जाती है। चयनित विद्यार्थियों को छात्रवृत्ति की राशि (₹12,000 प्रति वर्ष) का वास्तविक वितरण 'कक्षा IX' (कक्षा 9) से प्रारंभ होता है और यह कक्षा 10, 11 और 12वीं तक (कुल 4 वर्षों के लिए) प्रत्यक्ष लाभ अंतरण (DBT) के माध्यम से जारी रहता है। अतः सही उत्तर कक्षा IX है।

questions.question_english: A candidate applying for an educational or administrative post under the EWS quota submits an Income and Asset Certificate. Which of the following residential property assets will automatically disqualify the candidate from claiming EWS status under Central Government guidelines?
options_english: A residential flat of 800 sq. ft.
A residential flat of 1000 sq. ft. and above
A residential plot of 80 sq. yards in a notified municipality
A residential plot of 150 sq. yards in areas other than notified municipalities
questions.explanation_english:
According to DoPT Office Memorandum No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) dated 31 January 2019, specific residential asset thresholds lead to disqualification from the EWS category:

1. Residential Flat: A flat of 1000 sq. ft. and above is an absolute disqualifier. Therefore, an 800 sq. ft. flat is permissible (does not disqualify), but a flat of 1000 sq. ft. or more results in immediate exclusion.
2. Residential Plot in Notified Municipalities: The disqualifying limit is 100 sq. yards and above. An 80 sq. yard plot falls safely below the ceiling.
3. Residential Plot in Non-Notified Areas: The disqualifying limit is 200 sq. yards and above. A 150 sq. yard plot falls safely below the ceiling.

Thus, only the ownership of 'a residential flat of 1000 sq. ft. and above' acts as an automatic statutory bar to claiming EWS reservation.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the operation of a post-based reservation roster:
I. The number of reserved points in the roster is directly proportionate to the prescribed statutory percentage of reservation.
II. The roster operates continuously and infinitely, without being limited or squeezed to the sanctioned cadre strength.
III. Once the prescribed number of reserved posts in a cadre is fully occupied, the roster becomes temporarily inoperative for that category until a corresponding vacancy arises.
Which of the statements given above correctly describe the post-based roster system?
questions.explanation_english:
Under the post-based roster system established pursuant to the R.K. Sabharwal judgment (1995) and DoPT OM dated 2nd July 1997: 
1. Statement I is correct: Points in the roster are earmarked strictly to reflect the exact percentage of reservation prescribed for SC (15%), ST (7.5%), OBC (27%), and EWS (10%).
2. Statement II is incorrect: A post-based roster does NOT run infinitely. It is strictly bounded, mapped, and squeezed to the total sanctioned cadre strength (number of posts) in that specific cadre. 
3. Statement III is correct: Once the quota for a reserved category has reached the sanctioned ceiling within the cadre, the reservation roster stops operating for that category. Future appointments cannot be made from that reserved category against unreserved vacancies until an incumbent of that reserved category vacates a post. Hence, statements I and III are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आर.के. सभरवाल निर्णय (1995) और 2 जुलाई 1997 के DoPT कार्यालय ज्ञापन के तहत पद-आधारित रोस्टर प्रणाली के अनुसार:
1. कथन I सही है: रोस्टर में आरक्षित बिंदुओं की संख्या संबंधित श्रेणियों (SC-15%, ST-7.5%, OBC-27%, EWS-10%) के लिए निर्धारित वैधानिक प्रतिशत के अनुपात में होती है।
2. कथन II गलत है: पद-आधारित रोस्टर अनंत रूप से नहीं चलता, बल्कि यह संवर्ग के कुल स्वीकृत पदों (cadre strength) तक ही सीमित और आबद्ध (squeezed) होता है।
3. कथन III सही है: जब किसी संवर्ग में किसी आरक्षित वर्ग के सभी निर्धारित पद भर जाते हैं, तो रोस्टर उस श्रेणी के लिए तब तक निष्क्रिय रहता है जब तक कि उस श्रेणी का कोई पद रिक्त न हो जाए। अतः केवल कथन I और III सही हैं।

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): An SC candidate who qualifies the CTET by availing the 5% relaxation in qualifying marks, but scores higher than the general cut-off marks in the final recruitment exam, is counted against an unreserved (UR) vacancy.
Reason (R): Under established service jurisprudence and DoPT guidelines, candidates who avail relaxation in eligibility criteria or standards of suitability (such as qualifying exam marks) are adjusted against reserved vacancies, as they are not treated as "Own Merit" candidates for unreserved quota adjustment.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: The Supreme Court of India in landmark judgments such as Deepa E.V. v. Union of India (2017), Niravkumar Dilipbhai Makwana v. Gujarat Public Service Commission (2019), and Gaurav Pradhan v. State of Rajasthan (2018), along with DoPT OM No. 36012/13/88-Estt.(SCT), has settled the legal principle of Meritorious Reserved Candidates (MRC) / Own Merit Candidates. A reserved category candidate can migrate to and be adjusted against an Unreserved (UR) open vacancy only if they have qualified on their own merit without availing any relaxation in eligibility criteria, age limit, experience, or minimum qualifying marks in preliminary/screening eligibility tests (such as CTET). Since the SC candidate availed the 5% relaxed standard in CTET to become eligible, they cannot be considered an 'own merit' candidate and must strictly be adjusted against the SC quota, regardless of how high their score was in the subsequent recruitment exam. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false, whereas Reason (R) is true and correctly articulates service law.
questions.explanation_hindi: माननीय सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा 'दीपा ई.वी. बनाम भारत संघ (2017)' तथा 'नीरवकुमार दिलीपभाई मकवाना बनाम गुजरात लोक सेवा आयोग (2019)' जैसे ऐतिहासिक निर्णयों तथा DoPT के कार्यालय ज्ञापन के अनुसार, केवल उन्हीं आरक्षित श्रेणी के उम्मीदवारों को अनारक्षित (UR) मेरिट सूची में समायोजित किया जा सकता है जिन्होंने चयन प्रक्रिया के किसी भी चरण में कोई भी छूट (जैसे आयु सीमा, अनुभव या CTET जैसी प्रारंभिक/अर्हक परीक्षा के न्यूनतम उत्तीर्ण अंकों में छूट) न ली हो। यदि किसी SC उम्मीदवार ने CTET में 5% अंक छूट का लाभ लेकर न्यूनतम पात्रता हासिल की है, तो उसे 'ओन मेरिट' (Own Merit) उम्मीदवार नहीं माना जा सकता, भले ही मुख्य भर्ती परीक्षा में उसके अंक सामान्य वर्ग की कट-ऑफ से अधिक क्यों न हों। उसे अनिवार्य रूप से SC आरक्षित कोटे में ही समायोजित किया जाएगा। अतः अभिकथन (A) असत्य (गलत) है, जबकि कारण (R) सत्य (सही विधिक सिद्धांत) है। इसलिए विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: The historic transition from a "vacancy-based" reservation roster to a "post-based" reservation roster in Indian public employment was mandated by which landmark Supreme Court judgment?
options_english: R.K. Sabharwal v. State of Punjab (1995)
M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore (1963)
T. Devadasan v. Union of India (1964)
Ashok Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008)
questions.explanation_english: In the landmark Constitution Bench ruling of R.K. Sabharwal v. State of Punjab (1995) 2 SCC 745, the Supreme Court held that the reservation roster must be operated on the basis of total posts in a cadre (post-based) rather than on recurring vacancies (vacancy-based). The Court ruled that once the prescribed percentage of posts allocated to a reserved category is achieved in a cadre, the roster becomes inoperative for that category, and subsequent appointments against vacancies arising from retirements/resignations of general category candidates cannot be usurped by reserved category candidates. To implement this binding constitutional principle, the DoPT issued OM No. 36012/2/96-Estt (Res) on 2nd July 1997, replacing vacancy-based rosters with post-based model rosters across all central establishments.
questions.explanation_hindi: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की संविधान पीठ ने 'आर.के. सभरवाल बनाम पंजाब राज्य (1995) 2 SCC 745' के ऐतिहासिक मामले में यह व्यवस्था दी कि आरक्षण रोस्टर आवर्ती रिक्तियों (vacancy-based) के बजाय संवर्ग में कुल स्वीकृत पदों (post-based) के आधार पर संचालित होना चाहिए। न्यायालय ने स्पष्ट किया कि जब किसी संवर्ग में किसी आरक्षित वर्ग के लिए निर्धारित कोटा पूरा हो जाता है, तो रोस्टर उस वर्ग के लिए निष्प्रभावी हो जाता है। इसके पश्चात कार्मिक एवं प्रशिक्षण विभाग (DoPT) ने 2 जुलाई 1997 को ऐतिहासिक कार्यालय ज्ञापन जारी कर सभी केंद्रीय विभागों और संस्थानों में पद-आधारित रोस्टर प्रणाली अनिवार्य रूप से लागू की।
